minutes.headline: Select Board backed demolishing the old primary school for a town green and voted to pursue assessments and a spring article.
minutes.summary: The board held a workshop on the old primary school building and land, reviewing ranked-choice results of the informal town poll that favored a town green. Members debated the Architectural Preservation District's power over demolition and how to fund assessments. Two motions were taken by voice vote, and the town manager was asked to report on funding next meeting. Routine items covered DPW vacancies, a Complete Streets grant, and Brownfields funding for 925 Mass Ave.

public_comment.topic: Resident asked why the Charter is still not certified or sent to the legislature, worried the Parks Commission seat change cannot go on the spring ballot.
Resident urged doing the hazardous waste assessment now rather than waiting for the article, said the structural assessment is a waste if demolishing, and suggested historical plaques on the site.
Resident asked for a hand count at Town Meeting votes and said the APDC bylaw lacks a process for relief from an absolute demolition denial.

what_happened.line: The Select Board held a workshop on the old primary school building and land, reviewing ranked-choice results of an informal town poll that favored a town green.
The board took a voice vote to do a hazardous waste assessment on the old primary building if funds are available; the minutes do not record an audible tally.
The board took a voice vote to create a warrant article funding demolition estimates and design of a future town green on the site; the tally was not audible.
The town manager was asked to re-examine the facilities budget and report on funding for the assessments by the next meeting.
Earlier items included Brownfields funding for a site assessment at 925 Mass Ave and a full Complete Streets grant award to the town.

why_it_matters: Demolishing and replacing the old primary site with a green would need money appropriated at Town Meeting, so residents may be asked to vote on a warrant article, and the assessments could draw on a facilities budget while the snow and ice budget is already in deficit.
watch_next: The town manager's report on funding for the hazardous waste and structural assessments, due at the next Select Board meeting.
A member's facts-based letter on the old primary site, to be reviewed by the board the following week.
